answer: On a river bend, each dyer keeps one grinding stone that turns a relic mineral vein into pigment. The dyer registers the stone with the mill keeper, grinds one dated batch each week, and pours it into a settling tank where the keeper reads the ripple rings to check the grind matches the registered stone. A second stone under the same name voids both batches and bars the dyer for a season. To fake a thousand names, an attacker must build a thousand grinding stones, grind a thousand dated batches, and pass a thousand tank readings that all match.
